# AtomSQL: Interactive Disambiguation of NL-to-SQL via User-Guided Atom-Level Alignment

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#atomsql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol19/p4514-mazumder.pdf) · PVLDB 19(12), pp. 4514-4517, 2026 demonstration

**Reading coverage:** All four pages, Sections 1-3, equations, worked example and Figure 1; rendered Figure 1 inspected. No appendices.

## Research question

Whole-query confidence obscures which predicates, joins or modifiers encode competing interpretations of an underspecified request.

## Method

Runs several SQL generators, aligns clause-level SQL atoms with question phrases, combines model agreement with a per-user/schema preference matrix, and reranks candidate queries after user choices. Preference counts bias later selections without retraining generator weights.

## Evaluation

A demonstration scenario uses Spider’s student/pet database and a nine-step interface walkthrough. The paper supplies architecture and arithmetic examples, not a controlled user study, calibration experiment or benchmark comparison.

## What the results support

The interface exposes disagreement and lets users inspect alternatives before choosing a candidate. The paper illustrates how atom and model preferences change ranking.

## Limits and qualifications

Available interpretations are bounded by model-generated candidates; the paper explicitly requires reformulation if none matches intent. Agreement is a heuristic, not empirically calibrated confidence. The displayed SQL tree uses COUNT > 2 while the selected example discusses exactly two, so the walkthrough does not prove semantic consistency of every interface view.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful design for exposing localized ambiguity and recording preferences, with demonstration-level evidence rather than established improvement in user resolution.
